sample_construction: Select 14 sentences from the abstract, introduction, and Section 3 (Model Architecture) of the arXiv HTML/full text of the chosen paper. For each sentence, build text_a as the original sentence and text_b as a variant: (i) 6 pairs are assertion-preserving with only whitespace/punctuation/case or benign numerical restatement differences (gt=true); (ii) 6 pairs introduce exactly one assertion-level rewrite drawn from negation-polarity flip, assertion-tail deletion, or connector/concession change (gt=false); (iii) 2 pairs are near-duplicates with repetition or punctuation only (gt=true). Variants are drafted manually from the paper's own sentences. samples_blind.json will carry only id/text_a/text_b and no type labels.
criterion_induction: Induce a deterministic boolean judge that compares text_b against text_a at the assertion level: normalize whitespace and punctuation, then verify that every negation token, every assertion complement/tail predicate, and every concessive/connector cue present in one text is preserved in the other with the same polarity and scope; if any negation is flipped, any complement is dropped, or any connector is added/removed such that the claim changes, return false with character-span anchors; purely lexical or formatting differences return true. The function is pure: no IO, no randomness, no time, no hard-coded ids or labels.
gt_definition: Ground truth is defined from literal text facts before any criterion is applied: text_b is an assertion-preserving variant of text_a iff text_b can be obtained from text_a by only whitespace/punctuation/case/benign numerical restatement without dropping or flipping any negation, complement, or connector; otherwise false. Each gt is decided by manual inspection of the source sentences and recorded only in gt_private.json, never in samples_blind.json.
coverage_plan: Guarantee at least one dedicated pair for each of the three §0b phenomena: (a) negation-polarity flip — e.g., a paper claim with 'not' / 'never' vs the same claim without it; (b) assertion-tail deletion — e.g., a full claim with its complement vs the same sentence truncated after the main verb; (c) connector/concession change — e.g., a sentence containing 'however' / 'although' vs the connector deleted or swapped. Each phenomenon appears in exactly one pair for clean attribution; pair ids remain neutral.
